author: reek
body: CCE is the compiler's internal encoding and the boundary every piece of text crosses. to-unicode and from-unicode must be inverses wherever the mapping exists, so this counts mismatches over ranges rather than spot checking a few characters.

author: reek
body: It also counts how many points are MAPPED. Without that the test is vacuous: a from-unicode answering minus one for everything would show zero round-trip failures and look perfect, which is the same shape as a function that always answers the same thing.

author: reek
body: The four named characters are the ones CLAUDE.md documents, kept here because a rule in that file rests on them: the em-dash does have a CCE code point and does round-trip, while a carriage return genuinely does not map. If those ever change, the argument in the rule changes with them.
